summary: The auxiliary-constructor Scaladoc incorrectly equates a `null` argument with the absence of a default expression.

items.issue: `this(null)` passes `null` as the annotation argument; it does not establish that no default expression is recorded. In particular, `null` can itself be a default expression, and this constructor cannot distinguish that case from an asserted absence.
items.suggestion: Describe only the implemented behavior, e.g. `Creates a \`defaultArg\` annotation with a \`null\` argument.`
